newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit moves on buying for major corporate deal.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit moves on buying for major corporate deal.

text.p: The ringgit moved up in the afternoon on buying by a Hong Kong-based institution for a large corporate deal in Malaysia, dealers said on Friday.
They said the buying triggered dollar selling by several Swiss banks in Singapore around the 2.5020 level.
"Once 2.5020 was broken it triggered a lot of stop losses along the way," said a dealer with a U.S. bank in Singapore.

At 0700 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5003/13 per dollar, after hitting a high of 2.4995, against 2.5023/30 at close of Kuala Lumpur on Thursday. It was at 1.7716/36 per Singapore dollar against 1.7741/58.
"The ringgit is also aided by a rumour that Malaysia will report a trade surplus in August and some fresh ringgit/Sing buying," said a dealer with another U.S. bank in Singapore.
"I would recommend buying dollar at this level," he said.
Malaysia's trade data for August is not due until the second-half of the month.

Dealers said the large corporate deal which triggered the afternoon activity was probably German Deutsche Telekom transferring funds to buy 20-22 percent equity in Malaysia's Technology Resources Industries Bhd (TRI) for around 1.42 billion ringgit.
